## {.opening}

```{=html}
<div class="s1">

  <div class="section-label cyan">PERSONALIZED PROMOTIONS</div>

  <div class="s1-left">
    <div>Our model says</div>
    <div>this household</div>
    <div>will <span class="cyan">buy.</span></div>
  </div>

  <div class="s1-score">
    <div class="s1-score-number">82%</div>
    <div class="s1-score-caption">
      predicted probability<br>
      of purchase
    </div>
    <div class="illustrative-note">ILLUSTRATIVE SCORE</div>
  </div>

  <div class="s1-question">
    Should we send<br>
    the coupon?
  </div>

  <div class="s1-options">
    <span>YES</span>
    <span>NO</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s1-answer fragment">
    WE DON'T<br>KNOW.
  </div>

  <div class="s1-answer-note fragment">
    A purchase prediction<br>
    doesn't answer that decision.
  </div>

  <div class="disclaimer">
    Illustrative customer and probability — not an empirical result.
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.questions}

```{=html}
<div class="s2">

  <div class="s2-intro">
    One decision.
  </div>

  <div class="s2-q s2-q1 fragment">
    <div class="s2-question">WILL THEY BUY?</div>
    <div class="concept-label cyan">PREDICT</div>
  </div>

  <div class="s2-q s2-q2 fragment">
    <div class="s2-question">WHY THIS SCORE?</div>
    <div class="concept-label violet">EXPLAIN</div>
  </div>

  <div class="s2-q s2-q3 fragment">
    <div class="s2-question">
      WILL THE COUPON<br>
      CHANGE BEHAVIOR?
    </div>
    <div class="concept-label magenta">INTERVENE</div>
  </div>

  <div class="s2-conclusion fragment">
    <strong>Three</strong> analytical questions.
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.prediction}

```{=html}
<div class="s3">

  <div class="section-label cyan">PREDICT</div>

  <div class="s3-number">82%</div>

  <div class="s3-number-label">
    predicted probability<br>
    of redemption
  </div>

  <div class="s3-side">

    <div class="micro-label">THE BUSINESS QUESTION</div>

    <div class="s3-question">
      Who is most likely<br>
      to redeem next cycle?
    </div>

    <div class="accent-rule cyan-bg"></div>

    <div class="micro-label">THE REAL TEST</div>

    <div class="s3-test">
      Did it work on customers<br>
      the model <span class="cyan-underline">never saw?</span>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="s3-flow fragment">
    <span>PAST DATA</span>
    <span class="arrow">→</span>
    <span>MODEL</span>
    <span class="arrow">→</span>
    <span>UNSEEN DATA</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s3-punch fragment">
    Prediction succeeds <span class="cyan">out of sample.</span>
  </div>

  <div class="source">
  SOURCES&nbsp;&nbsp; Mullainathan &amp; Spiess (2017) · <i>JEP</i> 31(2) · p. 87
  &nbsp;|&nbsp; Kleinberg et al. (2015) · <i>AER</i> 105(5) · p. 492
</div>

</div>
```

## {.explanation}

```{=html}
<div class="s4">

  <div class="s4-score">82%</div>
  <div class="s4-center-label">ONE MODEL OUTPUT</div>

  <div class="s4-prompt s4-p1 fragment">
    <div class="role-label violet">ANALYST</div>
    <div class="s4-copy">
      What drove<br>
      this score?
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="s4-prompt s4-p2 fragment">
    <div class="role-label violet">MANAGEMENT</div>
    <div class="s4-copy">
      Can I understand<br>
      and defend it?
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="s4-prompt s4-p3 fragment">
    <div class="role-label violet">USER / AUDITOR</div>
    <div class="s4-copy">
      Why this<br>
      outcome?
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="s4-conclusion fragment">
    Different people need<br>
    <span class="violet">different explanations.</span>
  </div>

  <div class="source">
    SOURCE&nbsp;&nbsp; NIST AI RMF 1.0 (2023) · §3.5 · p. 16
    &nbsp;|&nbsp; Phillips et al. (2021) · NISTIR 8312 · §2.2 · pp. 3–4
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.opacity}

```{=html}
<div class="s5">

  <div class="s5-title">
    WHEN DOES<br>
    OPACITY MATTER?
  </div>

  <div class="s5-case s5-left">
    <div class="case-number">01</div>

    <div class="s5-case-name">
      GROCERY<br>
      RECOMMENDATION
    </div>

    <div class="s5-result">
      wrong prediction
      <span>→ less relevant product</span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="s5-case s5-right fragment">
    <div class="case-number">02</div>

    <div class="s5-case-name magenta">
      HIGH-STAKES<br>
      DECISION
    </div>

    <div class="s5-result">
      opaque decision
      <span>→ harder to scrutinize</span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="s5-spectrum fragment">
    <div class="spectrum-left">LOWER CONSEQUENCE</div>
    <div class="spectrum-line"></div>
    <div class="spectrum-right">HIGHER CONSEQUENCE</div>
  </div>

  <div class="s5-takeaway fragment">
    The question isn't simply<br>
    <span class="crossed">BLACK BOX OR NOT?</span><br>
    <strong>What does opacity cost here?</strong>
  </div>

  <div class="s5-rudin fragment">
    <div class="micro-label violet">A STRONGER POSITION</div>
    Rudin argues for inherently interpretable models
    in high-stakes decisions.
  </div>

  <div class="source">
    SOURCE&nbsp;&nbsp; Rudin (2019) · <i>Nature Machine Intelligence</i> 1 · pp. 206–215
    &nbsp;|&nbsp; NIST AI RMF 1.0 (2023)
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.intervention}

```{=html}
<div class="s6">

  <div class="s6-predict cyan">
    LIKELY<br>
    TO BUY
  </div>

  <div class="s6-not-equal fragment">≠</div>

  <div class="s6-intervene fragment">
    LIKELY TO BE<br>
    <span class="magenta">PERSUADED</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s6-example s6-a fragment">
    <div class="customer-label">CUSTOMER A</div>
    <div class="s6-prob cyan">90%</div>
    <div class="s6-desc">likely to buy</div>
    <div class="s6-outcome">buys anyway</div>
  </div>

  <div class="s6-example s6-b fragment">
    <div class="customer-label">CUSTOMER B</div>
    <div class="s6-prob magenta">35%</div>
    <div class="s6-desc">likely to buy</div>
    <div class="s6-outcome intervention-outcome">
      coupon changes decision
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="s6-bottom fragment">
    Predicting <span class="cyan">behavior</span>
    is not the same as estimating the effect of an
    <span class="magenta">action.</span>
  </div>

  <div class="source">
    SOURCE&nbsp;&nbsp; Kleinberg, Ludwig, Mullainathan &amp; Obermeyer (2015) ·
    <i>AER</i> 105(5) · p. 491
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.project}

```{=html}
<div class="s7">

  <div class="section-label violet">THE PROJECT</div>

  <div class="s7-title">
    Now put these questions<br>
    into <span class="violet">real retail data.</span>
  </div>

<div class="s7-stat-block s7-households">
  <div class="s7-big">2,500</div>
  <div class="s7-stat-copy">
    FREQUENT-SHOPPER HOUSEHOLDS
  </div>
</div>

<div class="s7-stat-block s7-years">
  <div class="s7-big">2</div>
  <div class="s7-stat-copy">
    YEARS OF TRANSACTIONS
  </div>
</div>

  <div class="s7-data fragment">

    <div class="s7-data-item">
      <span>01</span>
      TRANSACTIONS
    </div>

    <div class="s7-data-item">
      <span>02</span>
      CAMPAIGNS
    </div>

    <div class="s7-data-item">
      <span>03</span>
      COUPONS + REDEMPTION
    </div>

    <div class="s7-data-item">
      <span>04</span>
      DISPLAY + MAILER
    </div>

  </div>

    Enough to observe marketing exposure.<br>
    <span class="magenta">Not enough to assume causality.</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s7-warning fragment">
    OBSERVED<br>
    ≠<br>
    RANDOMIZED
  </div>

  <div class="source">
    SOURCE&nbsp;&nbsp; dunnhumby (2023) · <i>The Complete Journey User Guide</i> · pp. 2, 4–6
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.framework}

```{=html}
<div class="s8">

  <div class="s8-title">
    START WITH<br>
    THE <span>DECISION.</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s8-row s8-r1 fragment">

    <div class="row-number">01</div>

    <div class="s8-verb cyan">FORECAST</div>

    <div class="s8-question">
      What is likely<br>
      to happen?
    </div>

    <div class="s8-evidence">
      TEST
      <strong>unseen data</strong>
    </div>

    <div class="s8-method cyan-border">
      PREDICT
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="s8-row s8-r2 fragment">

    <div class="row-number">02</div>

    <div class="s8-verb violet">UNDERSTAND</div>

    <div class="s8-question">
      Why this<br>
      output?
    </div>

    <div class="s8-evidence">
      TEST
      <strong>meaningful explanation</strong>
    </div>

    <div class="s8-method violet-border">
      EXPLAIN
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="s8-row s8-r3 fragment">

    <div class="row-number">03</div>

    <div class="s8-verb magenta">CHANGE</div>

    <div class="s8-question">
      What will my<br>
      action change?
    </div>

    <div class="s8-evidence">
      NEED
      <strong>credible counterfactual</strong>
    </div>

    <div class="s8-method magenta-border">
      INTERVENE
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="s8-bottom fragment">
    Don't ask <em>"Which model is best?"</em><br>
    Ask <strong>"Best for what decision?"</strong>
  </div>

  <div class="source">
    SYNTHESIS&nbsp;&nbsp; Mullainathan &amp; Spiess (2017) ·
    NIST (2023) · Kleinberg et al. (2015)
  </div>

</div>
```

---

## {.architecture}

```{=html}
<div class="s9">

  <div class="s9-small">
    SO WHICH MODEL WINS?
  </div>

    <div class="s9-none-group fragment">

  <div class="s9-no">
    NONE.
  </div>

  <div class="s9-cross"></div>

    </div>

  <div class="s9-reframe fragment">
    That's the wrong<br>
    competition.
  </div>

  <div class="s9-system fragment">

    <div class="s9-step">
      <div class="concept-label cyan">PREDICT</div>
      <div class="s9-copy">
        find promising<br>
        opportunities
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="s9-arrow">→</div>

    <div class="s9-step">
      <div class="concept-label violet">EXPLAIN</div>
      <div class="s9-copy">
        understand +<br>
        govern
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="s9-arrow">→</div>

    <div class="s9-step">
      <div class="concept-label magenta">INTERVENE</div>
      <div class="s9-copy">
        learn what our<br>
        actions change
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="s9-final fragment">
    Different questions.<br>
    <strong>Complementary tools.</strong>
  </div>

  <div class="source">
    SYNTHESIS&nbsp;&nbsp; Mullainathan &amp; Spiess (2017) ·
    NIST (2023) · Kleinberg et al. (2015)
  </div>

</div>
```

## {.close}

```{=html}
<div class="s10">

  <div class="s10-small">
    ONE QUESTION FIRST
  </div>

  <div class="s10-question">
    What are we<br>
    actually deciding?
  </div>

  <div class="s10-rule"></div>

  <div class="s10-close fragment">
    MATCH THE <span class="cyan">MODEL</span><br>
    TO THE <span class="magenta">DECISION.</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s10-callback fragment">
    82% likely to buy<br>
    <span>still doesn't tell us whether to send the coupon.</span>
  </div>

</div>
```
